author: shawenswift06
text:
You mean to import your own playlists to Spotify for playback? That's easy. Spotify supports importing local files to it. You just go to Settings > enable Show Local Files > click Add A Source to import your playlist to Spotify. Remember that this is on the condition that your playlist is saved as local files on your computer. By the way, if what you want is to export Spotify playlists, try drawing support from a third-party
Spotify music converter
. It helps you to locally download Spotify playlists to the local folder without quality loss.

author: WiKiD
text:
Ok, so I'd like to bring to your attention three bugs, but first I'd like to bring up how I use the application and why it's important.
I have more than one Android tablet. Three, actually. All three of them have the UG Tabs application loaded. All three of them are linked to one UG account. This one, to be specific.
I use this app for my band's jam sessions. One tablet goes to my lead singer (Tablet A), another to my guitarist (Tablet B) and one with me (Tablet C), and I also have a laptop open for when we do recordings. The laptop also is logged into the UG website logged into this account.
Ok, so here's the issues:
1) When I add a song as a favorite, I hit 'synchronize' on my tablet (Tablet C). When I hit 'synchroize' on tablets A & B, I am expecting them to be updated with the song from Tablet C.
However, this does
NOT
work.  Tablets A & B need to search for the same song (hoping is the same version of the song) and than add it as a favorite manually. This is a HUGE problem!! As a band, when we work a song this slows us down immensely, and we don't get that much time to practice with our busy lives! Please have resolved ASAP!!
2)
Playlists do not synchronize at all!!
Just like problem #1, if we want to run through a setlist, we all need to go into each respective tablet, build our own playlist and hope for the best! It should be MUCH simpler! I should be able to build the setlet on my tablet, hit 'synchroize', than on tablets A & B, they just need to hit refresh and we should all be up to date!
3) Adding a song as a favorite on the UG website (on my laptop) does not synchronize it on the tablet. Same problem as #1 and #2 for me.
Please resolve! I am willing to pay a little bit more for this multi-tablet/laptop setup I have going on. If fixed we might actually be able to bring our tablets to our gigs instead of just our practice studio!

author: UG Support
text:
To get the same favorites on all your tablets and UG account, you should coplete the following steps on all your tablets one by one:
1. Go to the "Home" screen of your Ultimate Guitar Tabs app on your device (Tablet A for example).
2. Go to "Account".
3. "Sign In" with your Ultimate-Guitar.com account.
4. When asked "Do you want to synchronize Favorites with your website account?", choose "OK" (Wait until the process is fully completed).
Note: If you already have favorites on your device, the app will ask you to keep them (choose "Keep Tabs" to keep everything you have in your Favorites).
Then repeat the procedure on other two tablets.
The synchronization button will appear in your Favorites after this procedure. Use it for syncing tabs anytime in the future.
As for syncing playlists, unfortunately there's no such option as of now, it's just in our plans for future updates.

author: WiKiD
text:
Quote by UG Support
To get the same favorites on all your tablets and UG account, you should coplete the following steps on all your tablets one by one:
1. Go to the "Home" screen of your Ultimate Guitar Tabs app on your device (Tablet A for example).
2. Go to "Account".
3. "Sign In" with your Ultimate-Guitar.com account.
4. When asked "Do you want to synchronize Favorites with your website account?", choose "OK" (Wait until the process is fully completed).
Note: If you already have favorites on your device, the app will ask you to keep them (choose "Keep Tabs" to keep everything you have in your Favorites).
Then repeat the procedure on other two tablets.
The synchronization button will appear in your Favorites after this procedure. Use it for syncing tabs anytime in the future.
As for syncing playlists, unfortunately there's no such option as of now, it's just in our plans for future updates.
Thanks for this, however the 'Synchronize' button did not work on the other two tablets, the main one I used. It only worked when updating my favorites from UG account to my tablet, not the other way around. I probably should have started with that.
Also, this does not provide a good workflow
On Laptop:
- I add a favorite from the UG website on my laptop.
On Tablet, user is on the "Favorites" screen:
- User needs to click on Home
- User needs to click on "Account"
- User needs to click "Sign Out"
- User prompted to Keep Tabs or Clear Favorites
- User needs to retype User Name and Password
- User needs prompted with "Do you want to synchronize Favorites with your website account?" and needs to click 'OK'
- Tablet synchronizes with UG Website account
The tablet part needs to be done three times since I have 3 tablets. This is not good workflow. The part that definitely slows us down is logging off, and reinputting the user name and password. I'd have to have my guys type on the tablet, which I'm none too fond of.
Also not sure why "Do you want to synchronize Favorites with your website account?"  is a prompt, I am assuming whenever a user logs in and clicks the synchronize button, they would expect their favorites to be synchronized with all adds/removes/changes.
A better workflow:
On Laptop:
- I add a favorite from the UG website on my laptop.
On Tablet, user is on the "Favorites" screen:
- User clicks on the "..." button
- User clicks "Synchronize" button
- User prompted with a question: "Do you wish to update tablet with 'Adds', 'Updates' and 'Removes' ?"
- User checks their preferences (if they want the Adds, Updates and Removes') and clicks OK.
- Tablet synchronizes with UG Website account
Thanks, let me know if you have any questinos!

Has anyone seen this problem or know how to get around it?
When using a bluetooth device for pedal mapping other than an Airturn, the keyboard won't show when clicking on the search text box making search unusable. The only way to use search is to disable the pedal, do the search, and then reenable it which is very cumbersome to search for a song.
Steps to reproduce:
1. on iPad using the iOS app

3. Launch the Ultimate Guitar App
4. Navigate to Pedal Interface in settings
5. Try to setup a pedal keys without airturn enables (nothing happens)
6. Enable Airturn Support and select the Keyboard option
7. map pedals to commands (this works)
8. Exit settings
9. Launch a playlist or song (pedal mappings will work)
10. Try to search for a new song, Keyboard won't launch making search unusable
This problem doesn't happen with Airturn pedals.

author: murrayphobbs
text:
Hi all. Been using UG for years to check chords and such from time to time. Only just recently became a contributor and only because some of my favourite Fred Eaglesmith songs were missing from UG. I use a desktop. I long ago stopped using my android devices to access UG because of the unrelenting spam that used to come through.
So, having just contributed 7 songs, as I was going to bed last night my phone beeped and I see a new email from UG saying congrats etc. I clicked on the link in the email and looked at my brand new entry then I scrolled down.
Then a very VERY nasty phishing page popped up on my screen - very slick - looked like HTML5 - telling me my phone had visited a website that had infected my phone, causing permanent and irreparable damage. Being a bit sleepy (and susceptible, hey i'm old) I was a bit freaked out but I ignored the page and closed it which revealed a very official looking Google website making the same claim about my phone - it wasn't google - it was part of the same very clever phishing scam.
Now, strikes me that UG is heading for some real trouble including some nasty litigation - had I suffered a heart attack or such at that point the coroner would have pized my phone from my dead hand to show the add still there and a clear traceback to UG.
Now that would be the extreme I'm sure but it is a real risk nonetheless - and that's before we get to what might happen if all those Android using UG fans out there get a meme going on social media or such that frightens people away from using UG.
Now this was not a UG phone app - this was the UG website recognising I was coming in on a phone and switching to some clever HTML5 type behaviour tailored to the phone OS/web app - In the past the thing I'd see would be the full page blurb about loading the UG app (which I made the gross mistake of doing once but never again as it was the most spam ridden app i'd ever loaded on my phone)
that blurb I could live with - skipping it and continuing to the UG web page
but this phishing thing was down right criminal - and I do not exagerate - I guess it was some sort of adversing channel UG makes money out of that UG is not monitoring or UG does not have control of and hence may even be completely unaware of
But it's bad UG - very bad, dangerous and scarey - you need to do something about it because as the old British Airways research says - it costs 5,000 times as much to win back a lost client as it does to get a new one.

the important bit of the email though is this link - this is the link that I clicked the other night to go see my brand new UG contribution:
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/components/email/go/?message_id=ug_f674563ca88df8cb9f6b7474989277df7244f12c&url=aHR0cHM6Ly90YWJzLnVsdGltYXRlLWd1aXRhci5jb20vdGFiL2ZyZWRfZWFnbGVzbWl0aC9rYXRpZV9jaG9yZHNfMjI2ODIxNw%3D%3D&hash=345f62d2891c56a2575e4e5a515f21c75ce85b16

So I clicked on that link and it took me straight to my new song - which looked just fine. It was when i scrolled down to see more that the splash page popped up with the nasty phishing page
now, here's what i think are the possibilities:
1. You incorporate some kind of advertising revenue library calls in the mobile version of your web site - and you have little or no control as to what is being fed into that system because the org you are using has very poor security and quality control itself - tsk tsk - give them a very hard time or ditch them and choose a similar service that's not a clone of the sort of stuff you get on porn sites and the pirate bay sort of thing

Your dev team does not include anyone that knows the whole system inside out - it's made up of folk who try hard but struggle with all the original code and so are a bit lost as to what to do etc and anyway most of the company's focus is in the legal department so the code team is a bit neglected

author: tjggriffin1
text:
Your library is so comprehensive that a search can generate a massive list. On the mobile website, the page selector at the bottom of each page only lets one move by one page at a time (more below). I searched for "Ages and Ages," then selected "A." I went through six pages before I got beyond bands starting with "A."  I had 6 more letters, at who knows how many pages per letter, before getting to "Ag."
I am certain it has to do with how the main site is formatted for mobile screen, so I don't know if it can be fixed. But if you can pass this on to your web developers, that would be much appreciated.
Problem: There are selector buttons for 3 pages + previous and next pages. Like this:
First page:
[1] [2] [3] [Next >]
0ther pages:
[< Prev] [27] [28] [29] [Next >]
Last of 56 pages:
[< Prev] [53] [54] [55]
Except for the first and last page, the current page is in the middle. This means there are redundant buttons. On the first page, '2' and 'Next,' do exactly the same thing. On the last page, it's 'Prev'  and '54' (or '53'). On other pages,  the are 2 pairs of redundant buttons: 'Prev' and '27  and  '29' and 'Next.'
Solution: I suggest having 5 page numbers, previous, next, beginning and end, like:
[1] [2] [3] [4] [5]  [5 >]  [>>]
[<<]  [< 5]  [26] [27] [28] [29] [30]  [5 >]  [>>]
[<<]  [< 5]  [51] [52] [53] [54] [55]
If the total number of psges isn't a multiple of 5, then something like:
[<<]  [< 5]  [51] [52] [53] [54] [55]  [2 >]
followed by:
[<<]  [< 5]  [56] [57]
Having fiter and sorting options beyond the alphabet would be very helpful.
Also, if you could put the selector at the top and the bottom of the page, that would be helpful as well. Sometimes you know you want to go on without going to the bottom of the page.
The app doesn't have this problem. When one gets to bottom of the page, but not the end of the list, the next page is auto-loaded, And scrolling is fast.  The full website has plenty of room for a dozen or so page numbers.
Thank you for bearing with me, and for considering my suggestions.

I think you might be confusing “repeat bar” symbols with “repeat signs”.  Look for measures that have an oblique line or two in the middle, and a dot both above and below the line(s).  One line means repeat the previous bar, and 2 lines means repeat the previous two bars.

author: kroony
text:
After a lot of ****ing around I have a solution.
on my android i navigate to Internal storage\Android\data\com.ultimateguitar.tabs\favorites
in that folder are 100's of files named similar to this 123.fav. I suspected that file name is the database ID of the tab but just had to find somewhere on the site to put it in to access it.
If you take this url
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/home/favorites/?tabs&act=addtab&fid=
and type in the number from one of those files at the end, eg:
https://www.ultimate-guitar.com/home/favorites/?tabs&act=addtab&fid=4035
going to that address will add that song to your favourites if you are already logged in.
Its freaking laborious but there was no way i was going to remember 100's of awesome songs that i found.
Also for those that know what im on about, those .fav files on the phone are zip files. rename them and there is another .fav file in them that is actually java serialised HTML of the tabs

author: brent.rasmussen
text:
I recently switched over to using an iPad in live performances because I just can't see the tiny text on my phone screen any longer.
It works well generally, but when I am using "old guy mode" (huge words on the screen), some of the faster-tempo songs on my set lists cannot scroll fast enough to keep up with the pace of the song, even with the scroll speed set to maximum. I have to keep reaching out and scrolling the song manually with my finger, and that breaks my guitar rhythm line and looks like shit onstage.
I have a bluetooth page turner pedal that I am messing around with that is set to scroll-down one page with a click, and that's promising, but it's only a temporary workaround band-aid - it's not a solution to the problem.
The solution would be for your iPad UG Tabs app developers to increase the scroll speed limit on the iPad app. Give it a few more speed "levels" above (faster than) where it stops right now. That would be awesome.
I have no idea how to code, or how to modify apps, but it seems to this layman that something like that should be a relatively minor and simple change to make. Maybe I am wrong, I don't know.
In any case, if that change could be suggested to your app developer team, I would really appreciate it.
Thanks! Long-time UG user and tab author,
-Brent Rasmussen

author: mariaorwhatever
text:
Ok so I've been using Ultimate-Guitar for YEARS.... as in, well over 10 years (:
But I finally made an account literally just to post this because I'm at my wit's end.
A-Hard Rain's Gonna Fall came on Spotify, and I already had the Ultimate-Guitar app up, so I decided to learn it.
On a whim, I decided to press "simplify" for the first time. I don't know if the feature existed way back when I was a teenager, but I haven't ever needed it since it was formed. Maybe I just never cared to use it. Anyway, I come to find out it just takes away the bass notes/inversions, extensions, etc. Which I should've guessed.
Well... I left the tab I was on for a second, and go back to it, and do not see "Simplify". Anywhere.
Getting agitated, I decided to try something. I went to Fly Me To The Moon, as I knew it would have plenty of... not-simple chords, I guess you could say.
I pressed "simplify", and it lights up green, and allows me to undo the option. THEN, I pressed "simplify" again, left the tab, and go back to the tab again, and sure as the sun, it's gone just like it was on the Dylan tab.
Can anyone explain this to me? Has this happened to anyone else? Am I going blind or senile in my 20s and there's some simple (...no pun intended I SWEAR
) solution that I just could not find?
Anyway, point being, I really think this should be fixed. I get that the Simplify option is wonderful for beginners and intermediates alike, but I'm really glad to know to stay away from it now. And really happy that my first time trying it was on a song that I was just going to learn for fun.
So yeah. Rant over. Help would be greatly appreciated.

author: metelev.vladislav.ug
text:
mariaorwhatever
Thanks for reporting this bug. Managed to repeat it myself.
So while you can't turn Similify off on the tab page you could do so in the tab options (three dots at the right top corner): tab opetions -> settings -> simplify.
Hope this helps.

author: worldofgray
text: It is aggravating beyond belief to read through these threads and discover that countless people have been having the same chronic issue with this app for years without the UG crew actually fixing the problem. WTF did we pay for with our pro subscription?? I've had some good responsiveness in the past from the support team about other issues, and it's been nice to see the app evolve with its features and things over time. But this offline tabs issue is clearly of crucial and fundamental importance to a great deal of musicians - and I'm also now very confident that it's not just some weird fluke that's happening because my phone doesn't want to act right. Y'all need to fix this shit. It is not okay to charge people for a pro subscription and then completely fail to address a huge problem with the app that this many people have been having for this long. I hate to sound like a Karen or whatever, but when people pay for a service it is 100% natural to expect it to reliably function the way it is supposed to - and it is 100% your responsibility to fix it as quickly as possible when it does not. It blows my mind to see how many complaints have been happening for the same issue for this long without it being fixed. This is really bad for your reputation, which may not bother you since you don't really have much competition when it comes to apps like this - but it shouldn't be competition alone that drives your motivation to address the problems your paying customers are having with your product. For the love of God, please talk to your coders and get them to fix this. The app needs to have a permanent cache with an option in the app to replenish all downloaded tabs or something - and it also needs to pull up the saved version by default whenever someone has no internet signal. If this app was probably coded, it would not even think of giving a connectivity error when my phone is already in airplane mode with no Wi-Fi and I'm trying to pull up a tab that should be accessible offline. It makes no sense that this problem is going on this long for so many people. Argh!

Selecting song order in a playlist:

author: cheddargt
text:
Hello! First, i'd like to say the Ultimate Guitar app is absolutely fantastic! It is by far the cleaner, easier and better app for finding tabs and playing along to them I've ever came across to, but however, there's one little thing I think it's missing. so I'll leave it as a suggestion here.
The one thing that would make the app even
more
amazing would be:
custom tabs
.
How does it work?
You'd get like one single file as a "scratch" (so it would be able to save and syncronize on your profile and wouldn't overcharge the website's database). With it, you'd be able to copy a tab and modify it as you like (write down the chords, modify the lyrics, change chording position, etc)
Why is this so relevant?
1. I'm yet to find an efficient, light text editor with autoscroll on android, and I think this simple tool would bring a lot more attention to the UGTab app.
2. I've seen myself in really tight situations where the only available versions of a song weren't as I intended to play it, and the edited versions I've made weren't "uploadable" to the website for being too similar to the original ones. So I'd be stuck having to either play that "wrong" version or writing it down somewhere on my phone and having to deal with no auto-scroll when playing live for a crowd.
What is there to consider before adding this?
- "Open on scratch" button on tabs you visit
- recognize chord function (available in tabs throughout the website)
- being able to open your scratch just as any other tabs (with all the chords in the song displayed at the bottom, auto-scroll, etc.)
How could we possibly do this?
I think a simple yet efficient way would be to make a "copy" of the "upload your tab" page and make it mobile-friendly inside the app. From there, instead of "upload your tab" there would be a "save scratch" button.
Why should it be limited to 1 scratch?
It shouldn't! I mean, that's up for you guys to decide... I think it would be cool if you were able to make more than one scratch, but I'm not sure it would be viable for the development team to do it... What I really would like to see is a "
level up in the Ultimate Guitar website to unlock more scratches available!
", in my opinion this would increase people's will to contribute and also make this cool little leveling up game
Well, that's my suggestion! Let me know what you guys think and if it is a doable thing! Cheers!

[h]
Solution 1
[/h]
Solution 1 is to "force stop" the Google Play Store app. This should force it to refresh the versions of apps available to you. The below steps may vary slightly from device to device, but you should still be able to do this on any Android device.
Open your device settings.
Go to the settings page where you can view all of your apps.
Search or select the Google Play Store.
Tap the "Force Stop" button. See the image below for an example of what the force stop button may look like for you.
Reopen and find Safepoint on the Google Play Store, it should show a newer version if one is available. If this doesn't work, try the next solution below.
Solution 2
Solution 2 is to clear any data that the Google Play Store may have stored and force it to re-request it. Don't worry, this shouldn't affect any of your existing apps. Again, the below steps may vary slightly from device to device, but you should still be able to do this on any Android device.
Open your device settings.
Go to the settings page where you can view all of your apps.
Search or select the Google Play Store.
You should have a "Storage" (or similar) option.
Tap "Clear Cache" and then tap "Clear Data". You may see a warning pop-up, but again, don't worry as this will only clear the Google Play Store's data which we will refresh in the next step. Tap "OK" on any warning pop-up to clear the data. The image below shows an example of the page that you are looking for.
Reopen and find Safepoint on the Google Play Store, it should show a newer version if one is available. If this doesn't work, try the next solution below.
Solution 3
Hopefully, the above solutions have solved the problem, but if not, the last option to try is to simply turn your phone off and on again. Once your phone has restarted, search for Safepoint on the Google Play Store and you should see the newest version.

Hello there! You can increase the font size easily, just open a tab and find the "font" button. There will be two A's, one is bigger, another one is smaller. author: btopps
text:
This applies to both the mobile app and the website. Please add the ability to view two parts simultaneously. In GuitarPro, you can select and view multiple parts (probably would not be practical to have more than 2, but might just leave that up to the user). This would make it much easier to learn these elements completely and better replicate how they'd be played in a live setting.

Full disclaimer here - I work for Flic. Flic (flic.io) is a small wireless button that you could stick to your gutar and press while playing. We've had some requests about building support for Tabs (to turn pages/scroll) and Tonebridge (to switch amp). We would want that, but would need UG's support for it.
We've gained a lot of interest for turning page on sheet music apps such as forScore and Newzik, mostly within classical music and live orchestras.
To the community
- would you use a Flic button on your guitar to switch amps or scroll notes?
To Ultimate Guitar
- would you be open to work with us to make the integration possible? It would be an easy addition to the iOS apps, basically just listen to an external keyboard's right and left keys. On Android, it's a bit trickier.

author: tigermetal
text:
Hi
kgkicker
!
The new update supports Bluetooth and AirTurn pedals that are basically buttons that can remotely perform certain actions on your phone or tablet. You can find more info about these devices at
AirTurn's official website
.
If speaking about a looper—every iRig has an output port (a headphone jack), and you can use it to connect anything you want, like an amp or a guitar pedal. Treat "Tonebridge + iRig" pair as a regular guitar pedal that can be used in a guitar pedal chain. The input of this pair is the input port of the iRig, and the output is the headphone port of the iRig.
Hope this helps. Cheers!

author: johnharrisonford
text:
I like to use the ios app with this site.  I just find that it presents the tabs in a more useful way as well as having better accuracy as to timing.  I am missing the transpose feature, which I use to turn piano/vocal parts into things which sound decent on a guitar, as well as account for non-standard tunings (e.g. all strings one semi-tone flat).
I am not sure why this feature is unimplemented, but as a software engineer, I cannot imagine it being that difficult.  You can read tabs in a format, then draw and synthesis them already which is the hard part.  Transposing should be a matter of pre-processing the tabs, reducing each value by the requested amount of semi-tones and in the case you fall off the fretboard, shift the notes up one octave, and vice-versa for notes that are too high.
I get that this is likely a gross oversimplification, but it's a really important feature for me and one which is missing.

Hi!
As a keyboard player (mostly piano) I use UG exclusively for chords and I really love the amount of songs I can find here!
Anyway it is impossible to get proper flat chords when transposing a song.
If you need to transpose half a tone up a three chord song in D (e.g. D - G - A), you get D# - G# - A#. This is correct, but I'd really appreciate the option to chose flats against sharps (e.g. Eb - Ab - Bb).
IMHO, a simple way to achieve this, is to let the user override the default "transposition" strategy of OG and to specify the list of preferred tonalities. For example, in my case it would be: C, C#, D, Eb, E, F, F#, G, Ab, A, Bb, B
I bet a large part of piano players would stick with this... but guitar players could simply NOT override this and keep the "default" transposition strategy, which obviously is "C, C#, D, D#, E, F, F#, ..."
As a consequence, back to my previous example, when transposing +1 a D song you'll get Eb.
BTW, when transposing, any other chord in a song should respect the alteration of the final key.
What do you think?

author: UG Support
text:
ostar
the built-in tuner supports
standard tuning and a wide selection of alternative tunings
(drop, open, half-step down, etc.). However, at this time it’s not possible to tune strictly on a
per-note basis
inside the app — the tuner is string-oriented rather than a fully chromatic “note-by-note” mode.
If you need to tune to very specific pitches outside the available presets, a workaround would be to use a
separate chromatic tuner app
alongside UG. That way you can tune to any exact note you want, and still use UG for your tabs and play-along.
Your suggestion is definitely a useful one though — we’ve seen other musicians ask for more flexible tuning options, and I’ll make sure your feedback is passed along to the team.

author: kidrick
text:
As a user, what I want, is to set a scroll speed for a song and the song  should look the same for every device if I choose it obeys the standard  calibration. I shouldn't have to change it every time for every song  when I've already figured out the appropriate zoom (font size) and speed  for that song before. I should have the option to set the font size per  song instead of per device. I hate that if I have a song set up nicely  and then I come across a song with long sentences and I zoom out or even  accidentally change the zoom then it messes up every other song. The  scroll speed should also be set per song.
The ideal way it would work  is that I figure out the zoom/font size and the scroll speed (tempo)  for a song and it is the same every time I open it. I shouldn't have to  stop playing in the middle of the song to adjust it. If I switch to a  new phone or a tablet I shouldn't have to adjust every song too. It  should calibrate across devices so that if I've figured it out on my  phone, it should know the settings on my Mac/browser. If it's too  complicated to know the screen size etc of the devices automatically  then that could be done by a manual calibration I do that equates one  speed and size on one device to another and then it knows to apply that  calibration factor for all songs. That's as simple as having a  calibration page with 60 lines running the full width and asking me to  adjust the speed and size until 1 line per second passes. then doing  that on each device would give a conversion factor to know what the  scroll speed to have the same vertical displacement on each device. That  way I tell UG which device I'm on and all of my tabs will adjust  automatically so I don't need to calibrate it on every device. I can  tell each song if I want it to follow the standard calibration  rate/zoom, or I can toggle it allow a custom rate/font for that song.  The bottom line is that if I set up the scrolling speed once, i should  NEVER have to set it again regardless of the device. There should also  be a history of scroll/zoom states so that I can undo if I accidentally  change it. Here's a video from when I suggested it last year.
https://1drv.ms/v/s!AqTx1-ionvhqg6EVTX0U3ojCik_GzA?e=eJPRlT

author: phoenixvoice
text: I perform music several times per month, often for old folks homes.  Sometimes I use guitar; sometimes I use piano.  I often use paper chord charts/notes (when I need them), and I use the UG Tabs app on my iPad for a few songs, or when I switch instruments, and need to transpose the chords on the paper chart.  That is what happened today -- the paper chord chart was for guitar + capo, so I turned to the Tabs app so that I could pull it up and transpose for piano, and...nothing.  No data loaded in the app at all.  All of my "Favorite" tabs/chord charts are supposed to be there.  I finally turned on my phone's WiFi hotspot, gave the iPad internet access, and was able to access the "favorited" chord chart.  Meanwhile, my elderly audience had to wait several minutes while I navigated this.  I was looking into it just now and noticed the Tabs app needed updating.  I updated the app -- but the problem persists.  I know that I didn't have this problem one month ago.  Will this be fixed soon?  One of the features that I have enjoyed greatly with the Tabs app was the knowledge that I could bring my iPad with me instead of a heavy binder full of written chord charts.  Without offline access, I am going to have to start lugging heavy binders and books around with me again.

author: phoenixvoice
text: I just discovered that the app does -- eventually -- load the saved tabs/chord charts -- after more than THREE minutes!  So, basically, if I need to access a chord chart on the fly when the iPad is not at home I now have to fill three minutes -- the length of an entire song -- just waiting for my favorite tabs to load???  I would think that, as a workaround, I could just open it up before I start the performance but, no, that doesn't work either.  When the Tabs app has no internet access, it has the habit of re-opening when I switch to another app and return to the Tabs app.  (Maybe it is crashing?)  Then I have to wait another 3.5 minutes to get back to my hundreds of saved chord charts.  This app needs to work offline...otherwise, it is a fun thing to play around with when making music at home, but not much use in a performance situation.

author: phoenixvoice
text: And...I also work in IT, fixing problems, and I just seemed to have gotten to the bottom of this one.  Hopefully, others will also benefit from what I've discovered.  I often run a VPN for privacy reasons on my iPad.  When the VPN is turned on and trying to connect, but there are no WiFi networks to connect to, or WiFi is turned off, then the Tabs app takes over 3 minutes to load saved chord charts.  When the VPN is turned off and there is no WiFi connection, the Tabs app loads saved chord charts in about 15 seconds.  The problem appears to be some sort of network interaction between the Tabs app and the VPN.

Hi to everyone.
So I also got stuck with this issue. Just a few specs..
iPad 6th gen (software v14.4.2)
Airturn BT200 v2.3.1 475F
UG app v6.5.7
I always use the 1st setting on the pedal and struggled with the UG app.
After a search for the pedal settings to connect my pedal, it didn't pick up the pedal in the usual mode.
I changed the pedal to mode 2 (2 blinking red lights) and changed the airturn connection mode in the app to keyboard.
This is when your keyboard doesn't appear anymore.
So after this happened I deleted and reinstalled the app and the problem re-appeared.
But upon returning to the airturn settings I saw the Air turn settings my device appear in the devices list.
Clicked on it, it asked to pair, then I changed the connection mode to AirDirect And BAM!
Pedal works and my keyboard even appears without having to disable to bluetooth temporarily.
So in short.
Connect via the keyboard mode and once connected. Click on the device and change it back to Airdirect mode.
This is best I can remember.

author: UG Support
text:
Hello!
Ultimate Guitar Pro is a cross-platform service.
﻿​﻿
﻿Whether you purchased your subscription in our iOS or Android app, or on our website – you can use it on multiple platforms and devices.
﻿For this, you just need to log in to an account your subscription is attached to.
﻿​﻿
Note
:
If you registered with Google, Facebook, or Apple, you need to use one of these options to log in.
Do not use the Sign up with Google, Facebook, or Apple option instead of the Log in option.
​﻿
Can't log in to the app
If you were logged out of your account when you purchased a subscription in the iOS or Android app, it got attached to your device. In this case, only on this device, you can access Pro.
﻿​﻿
Here's how you can make your Pro subscription cross-platform:
﻿​﻿
Open the mobile app
Tap on the Account/Profile icon → Sign up
Go to settings again → Tap
Restore purchases
Next, you can use this account on all of the platforms to get Pro access

text:
Thank you for making the most helpful and useful app on my phone (maybe besides Google Maps) but still! Incredibly useful app thank you.
The Issue:
When the mobile app was updated a few years ago to the paid version, Tabs moved from a "1 to 100" Scroll Speed control bar to a "0 to 1.5" slider. This "1.5x" speed is way too slow for any fast moving song. Not to mention, if someone was near-sighted and needed to increase the size of the tab to be able to read it, the tabs would be much too slow for any song. I have great vision and I can keep the tabs as small as possible but still, the 1.5x is too slow for me in many cases. Please, bring back more speed control.

I also had issues with this but then i accidentally figured out what i believe to be a really good solution.   So, what i noticed is that if you click and hold the dot inside the speed adjustment while also nudging your mouse up or down of the dot and then quickly releasing your click you should see your cursor symbol turn into an "O" symbol with a slash going through the inside of it (disappears quickly once you release your click) which will mean that you can now adjust the speed without having to click and drag the speed adjustment dot anymore (just move your cursor left or right over the speed adjustment bar at this point to increase or decrease).  This makes it WAY EASIER for me to accurately adjust the tab speed (no issues quickly adjusting even .1 increment).
- ALSO, if you adjust your DPI on your mouse to a lower setting you can be more precise with your adjustments.
- You can also do the same thing as above but without moving your cursor up/down to enable the "auto hold" if you move the speed adjustment dot to the maximum or minimum setting and then click it and nudge your cursor left (if you moved dot to minimum speed) or right (if you moved dot to max speed).

author: afreedm1
text:
I noticed that there are a number of locked threads about getting the iRig Blueboard working as a pedal for controlling the scrolling of a tab in the UG Tabs iOS app.  I had been struggling for a long time to get this to work, and I finally found a solution, so I thought I would share it.  Although, I was unable to get the BlueBoard to scroll when connected through iRig's "Blueboard" app, I was able to get it to work when connected through another third-party app called
MIDI Wrench.
My procedure was as follows
Download MIDI Wrench.
Make sure the BlueBoard device is turned off and the iRig Blueboard app is closed.
Open MIDI Wrench.
Open the settings in the MIDI Wrench app (gear icon).
Turn on the "Run in Background" option near the bottom of the settings.
Choose Bluetooth MIDI, near the bottom of the settings.
Turn on the BlueBoard device
while holding down the "B" button.
This puts the device in MIDI mode, rather than it's native BlueBoard mode.  The blue light on the device will be flashing.
The BlueBoard device will appear in the MIDI Wrench device list.  Click on it to connect. The blue light on the device will turn solid.
Now close the settings and press the buttons on the BlueBoard.  The keys on the keyboard in the MIDI Wrench app should highlight.
Open the Guitar Tabs app and go to the Pedal interface settings.    Select one of the commands.  Then press a button on the BlueBoard.  The MIDI signal will now bind to the command.    Bind up all the commands you want to the BlueBoard buttons.  You will then be able to control scrolling using the BlueBoard.
The next time you turn on your BlueBoard, it will automatically start in the MIDI mode.  To connect it to the iOS device, just open MIDI Wrench and connect it in the "Bluetooth MIDI" setting.  It will then work for scrolling in the UG Tabs app.  To use the BlueBoard with Amplitube, you will need to start it in it's native BlueBoard mode by turning it on while holding down the "A" button.

author: afreedm1
text: Since this is a feedback thread, I'd like to make a suggestion to the UG Tabs dev team.  The iRig Blueboard is difficult to connect to UG Tabs because it is a Bluetooth LE device, rather than a Bluetooth 4.x device.  As an LE device, it can't connect through the iOS device's normal Bluetooth connections in the device's settings.  It must be connected through an app.  Other apps (such as the MIDI Wrench app) work with the iRig Blueboard and other Bluetooth LE devices by offering a Bluetooth LE connection feature directly within the app.  My suggestion is to provide this same Bluetooth LE connection feature within the UG Tabs app so that the third-party app is not required in order to use the iRig Blueboard device.  This feature would also make it easier to use other Bluetooth LE pedal devices.

author: UG Support
text:
To sync your favorites on both devices you should have online account at UG.com. Then just go through the following steps:
1. Go to the "Home" screen of your Ultimate Guitar Tabs app on your device.
2. Go to "Account".
3. "Sign In" with your Ultimate-Guitar.com account.
4. When asked "Do you want to synchronize Favorites with your website account?", choose "OK" (Wait until the process is fully completed).
Note: If you already have favorites on your device, the app will ask you to keep them (choose "Keep Tabs" to keep everything you have in your Favorites).
The synchronization button will appear in your Favorites after this procedure. Use it for syncing tabs anytime in the future.

Please let me know whether you've succeeded to connect the pedal to your device.

- The same chord variations.

It turns out that Google/Android/Chrome have multiple place to turn on or off opening web pages in apps. I turned one off, but didn't know about the others. Some of those were turned on. When I turned them off, it opens in the browser as expected. Here are some of them, in Android settings, except #3:
Setting > Default apps > opening link > Instant apps > Disable "upgrade web links"
Setting > Default apps > opening link > disable "Open links in apps"
disable "web and activity" in google account in chrome setting
Set as default > the apps (for example: reddit) > disable "open supporting link"

author: kidrick
text:
As a user, what I want, is to set a scroll speed for a song and the song should look the same for every device if I choose it obeys the standard calibration. I shouldn't have to change it every time for every song when I've already figured out the appropriate zoom (font size) and speed for that song before. I should have the option to set the font size per song instead of per device. I hate that if I have a song set up nicely and then I come across a song with long sentences and I zoom out or even accidentally change the zoom then it messes up every other song. The scroll speed should also be set per song.
The ideal way it would work is that I figure out the zoom/font size and the scroll speed (tempo) for a song and it is the same every time I open it. I shouldn't have to stop playing in the middle of the song to adjust it. If I switch to a new phone or a tablet I shouldn't have to adjust every song too. It should calibrate across devices so that if I've figured it out on my phone, it should know the settings on my Mac/browser. If it's too complicated to know the screen size etc of the devices automatically then that could be done by a manual calibration I do that equates one speed and size on one device to another and then it knows to apply that calibration factor for all songs. That's as simple as having a calibration page with 60 lines running the full width and asking me to adjust the speed and size until 1 line per second passes. then doing that on each device would give a conversion factor to know what the scroll speed to have the same vertical displacement on each device. That way I tell UG which device I'm on and all of my tabs will adjust automatically so I don't need to calibrate it on every device. I can tell each song if I want it to follow the standard calibration rate/zoom, or I can toggle it allow a custom rate/font for that song. The bottom line is that if I set up the scrolling speed once, i should NEVER have to set it again regardless of the device. There should also be a history of scroll/zoom states so that I can undo if I accidentally change it. Here's a video from when I suggested it last year.
https://1drv.ms/v/s!AqTx1-ionvhqg6EVTX0U3ojCik_GzA?e=eJPRlT

author: Niass

martin788
Glad it helped! Copyright holders forced us to add some ads for Pro Users. A small ad at the bottom of the tab was met with an expectable backlash. We removed it and added a promo line for these guys' affiliated guitar karaoke in a way that doesn't make anyone's eyes hurt.

author: martin788
text:
Niass
Showing ads to paying subscribers doesn't make sense, if a partner was to "force" you to do it then you should stop working with them.

author: Niass
text:
martin788
Unfortunately, we're unable to do that as legally they own almost all of our website's content and we have a choice, collaborate and pay millions of dollars to them annually or shut the site down.

author: martin788
text:
Niass
They don't have unlimited power because you are acting as salesmen to them and they don't want to lose you. Whatever their demands and your preferences you need reasonable conditions for your users, which include no ads for paying subscribers and authors. If you can't do that then you will stop being a usable means for us to exchange tabs, whether you officially shut down or not.
I would advise you to establish principles, commit to them and communicate about them, so that trust is established (or restored) and knowledgeable people are ready to invest some of their time. Trying to show ads to your paying users as you did is a sign that we are on shaky ground, which naturally prompts people to stop investing and start exploring alternatives.

author: ddzado
text:
I've figured out why it flickers. Obviously without having access to source code, I can't fix it.
It only flickers when the drawer max height is less than the number of instruments in the drawer. Meaning that if you can pop up the menu and the number of instruments fits in what the max size they let the drawer be it'l be fine. When you have more instruments that requires a scroll bar to be needed, this is when it flickers.
It most likely is caused by a conflict in values between the max height they allow in both of those scenarios.
I've complained several times. No response. I want to get hire for 1 week and fix the freaking issue.

author: methos1979
text:
I've been using the Pro version of the UG app for a few years now and for the most part it works well. They seem to have finally fixed the scrolling speed issue which is great. I still wish they would not SPAM me their ads for other services which can sometimes pop up when I'm gigging and is extremely annoying but for the most part as long as I remember to turn off the wifi I'm all set with that.
Two things that would really be helpful to the gigging guitarist that are available in other apps of this type are a built in metronome flashing dot and the ability to swipe the page left or right to go to the next (or previous) song on the playlist. Having to back out to the playlist and then select the next song is cumbersome and sometimes slow. This should be a simple thing that would allow fast changes to the next song.
As for the metronome, even a simple blinking dot at the top just to give me a count in speed to start the song would be fantastic. Ad these two things and you'll be that much better.

text:
Quote by davidjungling
Hello,
First time forum question, long time guitar player.
I am looking for an app I can play on an iPad at a campground while offline.  The iPad will NOT have cellular capabilities.
I paid for the UG Pro version.  Does this program allow me to display and scroll songs while offline?
There is another program called Guitar Songbook.  Works offline but is clunky to say the least.
I have read Q&As from this forum on this subject but everyone is all over the place.  Does work.  Does not work.  It may be a bug.
Could someone give me a definitive answer?
Thanks in advance.
Yes, it will work. You have save all your tabs as Personal, then you can access them offline. I typically save any tab I'm interested in as a Personal tab which I can then edit to my liking, change the key, add capo position, arrange as we play it, etc. Then I use this tab create my setlists. It will work offline. The one thing you have to watch out for is when you place them in setlists in a specific order you can sometimes lose that order when offline. I'm not sure why this happens. Generally I will create a setlist in the order I want and then the last thing I do before I leave for the gig is to check the order again to make sure it's correct and then I'll put the tablet (Samsung) into Airplane mode. When you lose the order you have to reconnect to the site to restore your order. I've had to do this at gigs a couple times by putting my phone into hotspot mode and connecting that way. But generally speaking you can definitely use UG offline if you are a pro subscriber, which you are.

author: herblay
text:
I love to play guitar and have folks singalong.  As so many songs are customized, or different versions have different lyrics / arrangements, I have to bring multiple devices, log in on all, open "My Tabs" on each.
We need a companion app for non-musicians.  In the perfect app, they should be able to:
View a user's My Tabs
Make playlists and push them to the user
Make a real-time "song request" or upvote requests other users are making
Sync their apps to the song lyrics, when I change a song
View other users in the vicinity, so they don't have to know / lookup usernames
Other options that might do the same thing:
Option for users to share "My tabs" with others
Option to share Setlists with other users (it would need to also send the songs)
Create a "Live Session", where users can tabs / setlists into a public "session" that other users have access to
Not sure what the best way to solve this is.  But I'd adore an easy way to give a group of people lyrics to songs I'm playing.

author: JamesRamos
text:
1.On the Applications menu, select Applications > Mail.
2.Select Create a new mailbox to start the setup wizard.
3.Accept the Nokia terms of service and select Start.
4.Select Mail for Exchange from the list of available account types, and then enter the following information:
- In the Password box, enter your account password.
- In the Username box, enter your user name, for example,
tony@contoso.com
.
- In the Domain box, enter your domain. Your domain is the part of your email address that follows the at sign (@) and precedes the full point, for example, contoso.
5. Select Next to continue. The setup wizard will try to automatically set up your email account.
6. If the wizard is able to set up your account, go to the next step. If this process can’t be completed automatically, you’ll need to enter your Exchange server name manually. In the Mail for Exchange server name box, enter your server name, and select Next. For instructions for locating your server name, see the Finding my server name section.
7. Select OK when Mail for Exchange informs you that it isn’t recommended to use multiple methods to synchronise your contacts with your phone.
8. Choose whether you want to synchronise your Calendar, Contacts, and Tasks by selecting the appropriate options and then selecting Next.

author: christoqher
text:
Here's an idea:
To see the images that do not show below open this google document:
Apple/Smart Watch App for Guitar Chords and Lyrics
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1QLer-3BYnR4rPJelv968JH5r6nRoOWRtNgPbQ-WoYhY/edit?usp=sharing
Image #1 (Home Screen)
Image #1 is a representation of what you would see when you open the app on your watch. It is a representation of the “playlist” created by the user on their smart phone.
Swiping left and right will reveal the songs they chose.
Clicking the “Start” button will start them from the song they are on.
(see Image #3)
Clicking the “List” button will take them to the “playlist” they created.
(see Image #2)
No force touch option. No digital crown scroll option.
Image #2 (Playlist Screen)
Using the digital crown (not pictured) or by swiping up or down, the user can scroll through their “playlist”
Tapping on any of the title’s will bring them to that song on the home page (Image #1) where they can click start to start from that song.
No force touch option.
Image #3 (Lyrics and Chords Screen)
Image #3 depicts what would show if you clicked start on the home page (Image #1)
The image will initially be static. Using the digital crown one can set the scroll speed (see Image #4).
Force touch will give you the options to go to the next song, previous song, up to the top of the current song, and home. (see Image #5).
Swiping with your finger up or down will scroll through the song, then resume auto scrolling at the speed set.
Tapping any of the blue chords will display that chord in detail on the Chord Screen. (see Image #6)Image #4 (Speed Set Screen)
Image #4 is a depiction of what one would see while using the digital crown from the Lyrics and Chords Screen (Image #3).
Turning the digital crown downward will increase the scroll speed, turning the digital crown upward will decrease the scroll speed.
The light blue arched bar will increase and decrease as the digital crown is turned.
The “x1.5” show above also represents the speed, this value will start at 0 and it will change as the digital crown is turned.
No force touch option. No scrolling or tapping options, once you stop using the digital crown the Lyrics and Chords Screen will reappear and after a brief pause it will begin scrolling at the speed set.
Image #5
Image #5 is a representation of what will show up when the user force touches the Lyrics and Chords Screen (Image #3).
Clicking “Back” will take them to the previous song, unless the current song is the first in their playlist then it will take them to the top. (Lyrics and Chords Screen)
Clicking “Next” will take them to the next song. (Lyrics and Chords Screen)
Clicking “Restart” will restart the current song currently displayed, at the scroll speed last set by the user. (Lyrics and Chords Screen)
Clicking “Home” will take the user to the Home Screen and leave them on the song they were last playing (Image #1)
Image #6 (Chord Screen)
Image #6 is a representation of what happens when the user clicks on any of the chords Lyrics and Chords Screen. A visual of the chosen chord is displayed.
Using the digital crown (not pictured) or by swiping up, the user can scroll through  variations of the chord (if applicable).
Tapping back will bring them back to the Lyrics and Chords Screen they left.
No force touch option.
Image #7 - how to use
By turning the smartwatch around on your wrist you can easily view the chords and lyrics as you play.
Especially useful for beginners that have to monitor where their fingers are, they no longer have to look back and forth and lose their place. And if they forget a chord, it’s only a tap away.

author: steven seagull
text:
I've seen a query like this before and I'm genuinely puzzled - what, exactly, is left-handed tab?
I understand that you hold the guitar the other way round but there's no "handedness" inherent in the tab itself - you don't read from right to left, do you?
I understand that basic chord diagrams ideally need reversing if you're a lefty because the'yre purely physical representations of the notes you need to fret. Tabs don't work like that though, the E string is always the E string, the 5th fret is always the 5th fret, and time moves from left to right. None of the things in tab are dependent on which hands you're using our which way round the guitar is.

author: jon.christopher
text:
When listening to backing track on iOS application and in chords mode, the lyrics scroll speed is too fast.
The application clearly knows where it is in the song b/c the current word of the lyrics is highlighted, however, the vertical location of that highlighted word changes over time.
Please adjust this so that the line containing the current word doesn't scroll off the screen!  I know this has been a long running issue trying to get the scrolling speed correct, but adding a "resistance" function would be trivial to do.  Here it is in python pseudocode:
def resistance(currentScrollSpeed):
targetYPosition = 20 # pixels from top of screen, adjustable
slowdownRegionHeight = 20 # pixels; only apply breaking when we're this close to the targetYPosition
offset = highlightedWordYPosition - targetYPosition
if offset < slowdownRegionHeight:
# we're getting too close to the target, slow down.
# speed is proportional to how close we are to the targetYPosition, if we've reached target height, this will be 0,
# temporarily stopping the scrolling
speedCoefficient = offset/slowdownRegionHeight
scrollSpeed = speedCoefficient * currentScrollSpeed
return scrollSpeed
This would apply a breaking/slowdown function to the scrollspeed such that the closer the highlighted word is to its target height, the slower the scrolling gets.  When the lyrics engine moves to the next highlighted line, the highlightedWordYPosition would increase, and scrolling would resume until it has to slowdown again.
Simple to implement and should fix this issue once and for all.
Thanks!

You can rename your playlist or delete it. Activation: long tap on certain playlist.

author: UG Support
text:
Before our last update of Tabs HD this app supports only text tabs. For Pro tabs usage we offered another app, Tab Pro HD.
New updated Tabs HD app also supports Tab Pro files. If you have already had subscription within Tab Pro HD, now you can restore it within Tabs HD. But if you haven't, you can buy new Pro subscription within Tabs HD (it can be shared in Tab Pro HD too).
Thus we have now two types of subscription in Tabs HD: Pro (unlocks text tabs, Pro tabs and Guitar Tools service) and Basic (old subscription, that unlock only text tabs).

To find any Lifetime subscription you should go to Apple ID account information in the iTunes desktop app, choose there «Purchase History/See All» and check your purchase list.
And anyway you have to get iTunes receipt, confirming your purchase.

author: kidrick
text: Since UG forces tabs to be of a certain format, it means that the scroll is inconsistent due to different spacing requirements for the lyrics and labels etc. Ideally I could have each bar of the sang be X number of lines long, but that violates the format standards and doesn't work when the spacing automatically moves down to the next line because of a large font size. A solution is a scroll speed marker that's embedded in the tab but not visible. So i put markers at each song section and tell the app the scroll speed or how long I want it to take to get to the next section. If the verse takes 52 seconds to sing, then I could put 52 beside the verse 1 label and it will take 52 seconds to scroll to the next label at the chorus. An elegant way to once and for all set the scroll speed once per song that works even when changing font sizes.

author: JerryWSegers
text:
I am frequently running the app over a satellite link and it causes problem with the interface.  It does not happen when running on a wired network.  To experience the problem:
1 - Get on a satellite link or other high delay link
2 - Go to the local Tab menu (It happens elsewhere as well. This is just the easier to explain the problem)
3 - Tap to select any entry.
I am runing an iPad Pro (12.9 inch)  iOS version 15.7
Take note the  the amount of time it takes to highlight the entry so you know it was selected.  It sometimes takes many seconds before the highlight appears.  By then I have tapped  the entry again because  I though it missed the first Tap.  I later find I have multiple instances open that I need to close to continue.
It appear that the program waits till it access something on the Internet before it updates the user interface.  I believe this is the wrong order to do things as it cause confusion every time anyone tries to use the program.
It seems to me that a better plan would be to update the user interface as soon as the  screen is  touched and start  an
Indeterminate prograss indicatior (Beachball for example) That is stopped when the process is completed and the requested.screen is displayed.
While this is a tiny problem with a wonderful program. I, and I am sure others, would appreciate the change I have suggested.
If perhaps this is some problem of my own making, please instruct me in how to avoid it happening.
Thanks

author: Jeff.Smart
text:
Dear Ultimate-Guitar-Team,
let me start of by saying that I'm a long time fan of your site, so naturally I bought the app a couple of years ago. I've grown accustomed to the seemingly endless stream of advertisement (even though I paid for the app?!) for features I don't really need - I can live with that. I can also live with the fact that about every three updates all my songs get kicked out of the app and I have to reload everything. Or the fact that every now and then the app forgets transpositions I made for a song, so I have to re-enter my settings for that song.
But during the last few updates it has become increasingly frustrating to work and play with your app. Features that used to work fine, have been changed for no apparent reason. Some examples are:
- I'm trying to listen to a song on my iPhone and play along with the app. Doesn't work, because the app automatically mutes any other music that is playing. Why?!
- There used to be a feature where you could hide the menu, so you have more space for the song itself. This is not possible anymore, so about 10% of the screen is constantly occupied with menu elements that I just don't need while autoscrolling a song. Why was that changed?!
- Font sizes and autoscrolling speed used to be saved specifically for the app for every song. Now Autoscroll-Speed is only set for the app, the website doesn't save this anymore at all (why not?!). And Font Size is saved across App and Website. But naturally because of the difference in size between desktop and mobile, my chosen font size for my phone is incredibly small on desktop so I have to keep changing it all the time. Of course I can zoom in on the app, but again the zoom level is not saved so I have to do it again for every song, every time. This is a major nuisance in the daily use of the app (and of the website for that matter)
- My favorite songs should be available offline in the app, but in fact sometimes - even when I'm online - songs just won't load.
None of these are catastrophic bugs but they're all just things that used to work a lot better on older versions of the app, which just makes me wonder - why change something that's working? Just for the reason of changing it?
It would be great if you could maybe take one or two of these suggestions to re-improve your user experience to the high standard that you already had achieved in previous versions of your app.
Thanks for taking your time to read this little rant.
Cheers
Philipp

author: UG Support
text:
Quote by musicforte
I have a playlist of about 200 songs, and it is all jumbled up, with no method to sort that I am aware of.
Is it possible to alphabetize a playlist without having to drag and drop every song to the correct order?
I am afraid that's not possible.   We believe that sorting songs in playlist manually is the best way.
Would you please tell why you have one playlist for 200?
What's the purporse of a playlist orginized alphabetically?
Your feeback would be appreciated.

author: musicforte
text:
I have several playlists for several types of gigs - not just one of 200.  For example, my playlists are made for different genres of music, or for when I play solo vs with a group.
I continuously add songs to my playlists at any given time, and as they grow (to 200 songs for example) I find that during a show, I might want to find a particular song that I already have saved in my favorites (perhaps in a particular key.)
Of course, I know I can just type the song name in to find it, but I prefer to scroll through my playlist to find it quickly.  As I do that, I not only find the song but it gives me a chance to see other songs that I have added as favorites that I might want to play next.
Another advantage of having an alphabetical playlist, is it makes it easy to compare with another musician's playlist (if we are trying to have the same songs.)  If they are missing something that we should both have, it becomes easy to spot.
Another advantage of an alphabetical playlist is for when I practice.  I alphabetize my Apple Music playlists, so having the songs in the same alphabetical order (again) makes it easier to navigate between the two for when I am listening and practicing.
I feel like there are many users that don't just create a playlist for one particular show (where they might play each of the 20 songs or so in order.)  For me, my playlists are more like specific fakebook collections, where I know all the songs in that particular fakebook are appropriate for the show I am doing.  And I'd like those collections to be better and more easily organized.
I hope my explanation was alright.   So what do you think?

author: UG Support
text:
Thanks indeed for explaining your approach to the feature.
Your feedback is truly valuable to our UX designers and is really appreciated.
We will consider adding alphabetical categorization in playlists in future releases.
Thank you for using UG!
Rock on!

author: map13790
text:
Having the ability to store charts "locally" to your Droid for places that have no wifi;  in my case my ASUS Transformer Prime, which I mount to my mic stand, is a wonderful thing.
While I am sure there are a bunch of other options, here is a work around for this that I've been using. It's called Evernote. A free Android app. Pretty simple really.
Once I've picked a chart I want to export from UG, from the menu item I select "Send By Email". I am then presented with several options. My list may be different from yours based on the apps installed on your Android device.
Google Drive
Evernote - create new
Gmail
Skype
Yahoo Mail
I'm sure if you use Drop Box or any or cloud storage on your Droid that would be present also. But this is about storing it locally to your tablet or phone.
Once I have selected Evernote the chart then loads into the app and I have the ability to edit out all the comments and any other text I don't want. I am then left with just the chart itself.
That's it.... I have not set up an Evernote online account but if I did I can synchronize it online as well.
Again I am sure there are other apps that would work just as well. Perhaps you prefer to save your charts to a PDF instead after you've edited it. I don't know about you but I always seem to be editing charts for accuracy, bass walk downs, etc not present in the UG tabs online.
Hope this helps
Mark

author: kwwaters
text:
First of all, I'm a loyal UG Tab Pro iPhone user; I absolutely LOVE the app - great work! Well worth the price, by far. I have almost completely learned to play from your app alone. author: Ian Paul Gint
text:
Quote by ke4mkl
I guess I should have said android tab pro favs. To online.
In order to synchronize tabs in the Favorites section of the app with your Ultimate Guitar account, you need to go through the following steps:
1. Go to the "Home" screen of your Ultimate Guitar Tabs app on your device.
2. Go to "Account".
3. "Sign In" with your Ultimate-Guitar.com account.
4. When asked "Do you want to synchronize Favorites with your website account?", choose "OK" (Wait until the process is fully completed).
Note: If you already have favorites on your device, the app will ask you to keep them (choose "Keep Tabs" to keep everything you have in your Favorites).
The synchronization button will appear in your Favorites after this procedure. Use it for syncing tabs anytime in the future.
Cheers!

author: rvelozo
text:
tigermetal
The expression pedal does not work. I think that it's because the way it sends the value changes. As the regular blueboard buttons are booleans, the expression pedal sends a series of values inside a range depending on how pressed the pedal is.
The blueboard works as expected! Compared to other apps it has a bank up/down that is usually assigned to the long press on A and B. That leaves short presses available to change 4 presets.
The ways ToneBridge is set Volume up and down are set to switches and not variable values.

author: karshnirajgupta
text:
Couple of years back I spoke with Eugene Lysy about the addition of Bluetooth pedals for using Tonebridge in live scenario. Now I can see that he implemented the switch external pedal function. But why is it so complicated. I wanted to use tone bridge in live scenario. Where I thought I will use Airturn BT 200 S 6 and will be able to use 6 pedals and I will be able to switch the pedals easily in concert scenario. However I just discovered that I can only use one button to go to the previous and another to the next pedal. But if there are 6 pedals in a song, and I have to choose 5th one from 1st then I have press the switch for 5 times which is complicated and might go out of time. Kindly check if this can be implemented. I want to program six pedals from a pedalboard to six Airturn switch channels so that I can select the one I need anytime and change it anytime to any other pedal.
I know you have already did something which is impeccable and we should not ask more. But if there are room for improvements then I think it would be best to make it invincible. I have few suggestion, I would be really greatful if this can be implemented.
1) Create two modes
i) Pedalboard mode - where we can assign pedals to individual switches rather than having their effects and volume control handy, as they are already balanced before we use it in live shows. In that case we will be able to use 6 different tones or any number based on the footswitches, the flexibility will be extreme and powerful. As you can see in any processor we can choose tones where the effects and volume level are set separately. It would be great if you could implement that.
ii) Keep the two pedal mode which is there now. Like volume up, volume down, effect up, effects down, Preset next, preset previous etc.
So that we could choose any one mode depending on our requirements.
2) the option turn pedal on or off is not working with switches. I want to assign a switch which will allow me to turn off Tonebridge effects, so that my signals can pass through this to a physical pedal board with or without tone bridge effects. By tapping on iPad it’s working but not from foot switches. Kindly check that as well.
3) there Is slight latency while changing from one pedal to another In iPad via Airturn pedal switch. Kindly check if that can be fixed.
4) *** It would be great if you could implement a loop feature. If loop start, stop, overdub feature can be introduced then it will achieve huge productive change as it will be unbeatable tool for practising and performing, it is already that though.
I know it is a lot, but could not stop myself requesting for these. I know you all are geniuses, you can definitially do these with absolute excellence.
Peace.
Karshni Raj Gupta

author: steven seagull
text:
Because the two app stores are completely separate - it's the same principle as computer sotware, just because you've bought it for PC doesn't automatically mean you'll get a Mac version too. I'm not personally aware of any paid-for apps that work cross-platform on mobile platforms. If it's a free app that runs off a subscription service then that's all running ff the same account, but if the developer chooses to or needs to charge for the app then it has to charge for it across all platforms, that's just how apps work. To put it in another context, if you're selling something in one shop you can't have it available for free in another.
Equally the iPhone and iPad apps will be charged separately because they are developed separately and work differently. If you've already paid for the iPhone app then there isn't actually anything stopping you from using it on the iPad too, however it'll just be an upscaled version of the phone app which won't make effective use of the iPad's larger screen. Although it's using the same content the two apps will differ considerably from a coding point of view, and equally if they're going to continue to support and update the apps then that's two separate, ongoing development streams.

To sync your favorites on both devices you should have online account at UG.com. Then just go through the following steps:
1. Go to the "Home" screen of your Ultimate Guitar Tabs app on your device.
2. Go to "Account".
3. "Sign In" with your Ultimate-Guitar.com account.
4. When asked "Do you want to synchronize Favorites with your website account?", choose "OK" (Wait until the process is fully completed).
Note: If you already have favorites on your device, the app will ask you to keep them (choose "Keep Tabs" to keep everything you have in your Favorites).
The synchronization button will appear in your Favorites after this procedure. Use it for syncing tabs anytime in the future.

author: UG Support
text:
brent.rasmussen
hello, thank you for your thoughtful suggestion! You’re absolutely right — with the rapid development of AR display glasses, there are exciting opportunities for music apps like ours to evolve in new directions.
At this time, our team does not have a solution or concrete plans in place for smart glasses integration. However, ideas like yours highlight an exciting challenge for the entire Ultimate Guitar team — imagining how features such as lyric and chord scrolling could be adapted for wearable displays in a way that truly enhances live performance and practice.
We’ll be sharing your suggestion with our engineering and design teams so it can be considered as we look toward future updates and innovations. Feedback like this is incredibly valuable for helping us understand where the community’s interests are heading, and we really appreciate you taking the time to share your vision.

author: entravo
text:
Hi everyone,
Just a quick tip as I could not find this anywhere and apparently some users in the community have been expecting dynamic connections between Spotify and UG apps but the Spotify development on this was frozen by lack of requests...
Several (many) songs have either wrong "listen" connections to Spotify for playback while you read the tabs or even none at all.
I Found that by renaming those tabs to the correct Singer/Author as tagged by Spotify, it populates the full list properly.
To illustrate, just try anything that is classified under "Misc Soundtrack" and you will probably be unable to play the song.
Rename it manually in your app or here in your account by following its Spotify title and Singer/Author and it will show instantly the music to help you practice.
+++
Dear UG dev team,
This is really a necessity with millions of Spotify connections.
As the naming convention of the songs it 'open', why don't you add a simple notice before ever new song submission like:
"MAKE THIS SONG PLAYABLE/RECOGNIZED BY SPOTIFY IN TABS HD BY USING THE EXACT SINGER + SONG TITLE FROM SPOTIFY"
That should not require much development and would definitively help the entire community... (and maybe cleanup your huge DB of songs if you send a quick note to missing correct title songs submissions).
Have a great day!

author: thegrim_sweeper
text:
Hello,
I teach guitar, have been for 5 years now. I use your app on a daily basis, and frequently suggest it to students.
I love the tab pro features, as being able to slow down songs, loop parts, ect are extremely helpful for teaching and learning. On numerous occasions though, I find myself in a pickle. I have 30 minutes to give a lesson. Say a student wants to learn slipknot or system of a down. We'd end up spending 2-10 min tuning down, which isn't really the best time spent for them. We could essentially learn the song with simple drop D tuning.  But to really learn it, you have to be able to play with it. I have apps that slow down and change the pitch of tracks, but the quality of the audio diminishes.
I'm suggesting the ability to modulate the instruments to a different key.
Since the app uses midi based instruments, it seems like a rather simple feature to add. Simple, yet essential to really aid in learning guitar. It makes sense especially given lower tunings require thicker strings, which "ain't nobody got time" to change strings for just learning one song.
To be clear
, I'm not requesting the ability to change tunings, but simply the key of the song. This would be just a simple modulation for the midi output.
Should it be global, for all instruments on the track?
Or intuitive for modulating only melodic instruments automatically?
Or should I be able to select the key for each instrument, like how I select Solo or Mute.
That's up to you guys.
I don't know if this is often requested. But I'm sure if it's not, and you did add it, it would be a blessing to many users.
Best Regards.

author: tigermetal
text:
Hi
jemenake
, Tonebridge designer here. We don't recommend to use any bluetooth tool with Tonebridge (or any other app that involves real-time processing). It's because the Bluetooth technology has latency—when you play a string, you will hear its sound from your BT headphones in 1/2 seconds or so — almost impossible to play that way. We tested it with several BT devices hoping for a miracle and obviously had no luck. Sad but true. Cheers!

author: johnnycanuck
text:
I use a desktop when identifying songs in Ultimate Guitar and editing chord sheets and for exporting them to text and PDF files.
For practice, I use songs that I've imported into Songbook Pro on an Samsung S7 tablet (I had to create Notepad++ macros to massage the text files imported from UG). I have a Donner Bluetooth pedal to *reliably* scroll as required.
I host a beginner drop-in at a local seniors center and I use a laptop, where I display an Excel index of songs, and then click on the PDF link to the song we're going to play and go into full screen mode. I'd like to migrate this to Songbook Pro, however the index sucks, and importing directly from UG on the fly is unreliable. These range from Hank Williams to Metallica.
As for 'video play' of songs, I download from YouTube and edit the songs in Reaper and play them on a Samsung A71 phone to my Spark 40 amp. My MP3 player supports pitch change, tempo change as well as STEM separation of vocals.
As for storing all my text file songs, they're now stored on my desktop in text based ChordPro format and thus interoperable and transposable.

author: tigermetal
text:
vimbai_87
hi! First question, what OS do you run Tonebridge on? iOS, Android or macOS? Second, Apogee One, as far as I know, has two output channels (left and right), and Tonebridge uses only one of them—so when the sound comes through another channel, you will hear no sound. We are working on a small feature that will allow to switch channels in this case, expect it to be out in a month or so (together with other cool features). Cheers!
